questions.question: Which protocol establishes a connection using a three-way handshake?
questions.explanation: TCP is connection-oriented and uses a three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) to set up a connection.

questions.question: Why is UDP faster and lower in latency than TCP?

options.A: It has no handshake, no delivery guarantees, and a smaller 8-byte header.
options.B: It uses a sliding window mechanism for flow control.
options.C: It guarantees reliable and in-order delivery of data.
options.D: It requires sequence numbers and acknowledgements for every packet.

questions.explanation: UDP is connectionless with no handshake, lacks delivery guarantees, and has a smaller header size.

questions.question: Which application layer service typically uses UDP because speed matters more than reliability?
questions.explanation: Video streaming uses UDP because speed and lower latency are prioritized over perfect reliability.

questions.question: How does TCP ensure reliable, in-order delivery of data?

options.A: By using an 8-byte header and avoiding handshakes
options.B: By utilizing sequence numbers, acknowledgements, and retransmission
options.C: By dropping packets when congestion occurs without notifying the sender
options.D: By treating every packet as independent and connectionless

questions.explanation: TCP guarantees delivery and order using sequence numbers, acknowledgements, and retransmission.

questions.question: What is the minimum header size of TCP compared to UDP?

options.A: TCP has a minimum 20-byte header, while UDP has an 8-byte header.
options.B: TCP has an 8-byte header, while UDP has a 20-byte header.
options.C: Both protocols share the exact same header size of 20 bytes.
options.D: Both protocols have a fixed 8-byte header.

questions.explanation: TCP has a minimum 20-byte header, whereas UDP has a small 8-byte header.
